children: If Albertans and Quebecois did vote to leave Canada, what would that mean for the rest of the country? Capital Economics' Bradley Saunders argues the blow to GDP from losing Quebec industry and Alberta oil and gas could be mediated somewhat by continued free trade, companies relocating from seceding provinces to the rest of Canada and a weaker Canadian dollar boosting export competitiveness in other sectors. As such, the economist expects the rest of Canada to outperform the two provinces, whose newfound independence would likely require fiscal tightening. Of course secession would be a lengthy and complicated process without precedent and as such there remains a lot of uncertainty, Saunders says. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)
